newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions pave way for possible strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions pave way for possible strike.

text.p: Argentine unions Tuesday gave their leaders the green light to call a general strike "when they consider it necessary" and the walkout might take place in January, a CGT union federation spokesman said.
At an hour-long meeting, a CGT central committee gave its directors the go-ahead to organize a stoppage.
The directors must meet to decide when the confederation's members will walk out.
The spokesman told Reuters that although hard-liners wanted a walkout this month or next, the widespread feeling was that early in the new year, after the holiday season, was a more suitable time.

"To call a strike now would be counterproductive because it is very difficult to mobilize the population en masse so close to the New Year's festivities," whereas successful strikes have taken place in January in the past, he said.
The CGT official said workers will march November 20 on the customs headquarters to demand a full investigation on widespread charges of massive smuggling and corruption.
The march will also be to protest government plans to reform labor laws, and to press for workers' demands for higher minimum wages and better pay for pensioners.
The CGT, whose unions represent nine million workers, held a 24-hour general strike in August and a 36-hour stoppage in September.

The CGT, a traditional ally of the ruling Peronist Party, has distanced itself from the government's austerity policies and its plans to reform labor laws, which unions complain would effectively make it easier for firms to sack workers.
